tapeLine: Monday 23 November: S&P 500 +4.73% (+326.78) to 7,237.17, back above 7,000; Nasdaq Composite +6.51% (+1,471.82) to 24,089.56, its best day since April 2025; Dow +3.01% (+1,447.98) to 49,595.31 (StockTitan; Motley Fool; FinanceFeeds, 23 Nov). One 24/7 Wall St. item has the S&P at 7,243.94 (+4.83%); sources differ slightly.
matters:
Monday reversed a large part of last week’s slide after Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, ten days after he resigned on 13 Nov. Nvidia closed +31.48% at $165.05 (Nvidia newsroom; CNBC; StockTitan, 23 Nov). The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government; President Trump told CNBC he personally intervened (CNBC; NBC; PBS, 23 Nov). Anthropic (ANT) did not join the rally, closing −1.43% at $87.64 (Yahoo Finance, 23 Nov).

Early Tuesday, futures were giving some of it back: at 5:50 a.m. ET Nasdaq-100 futures −1.21%, S&P 500 −0.50%, Dow −0.14%, with Nvidia down nearly 4% premarket; CNBC’s live blog showed S&P futures down about 1% at one point (TipRanks; CNBC; Globe and Mail, 24 Nov). After New York Fed President Williams said Monday evening that inflation is still too high and rates are likely to rise “over time,” fed funds futures priced a December hike as a certainty, up from 89% odds Friday (CNBC; TipRanks, 23–24 Nov).

calendar.event: Earnings: Dell (FQ3), HP, Workday, Autodesk; Best Buy before the open

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield closed Monday at about 4.92% (BondStats; Longbridge 4.9218%, about 2 bp lower; Investing.com 4.927%), 2-year 4.63%, 30-year 5.29% (23 Nov). CNBC had the 10-year at 4.908% early Tuesday (24 Nov). Dollar, oil and gold Monday levels not confirmed and left out.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Monday 23 November: S&P 500 7,237.17 (+4.73%); Nasdaq Composite 24,089.56 (+6.51%); Dow 49,595.31 (+3.01%) (StockTitan; Motley Fool, 23 Nov).

Nvidia — board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director; shares +31.48% to $165.05, after −14.01% to $125.53 on Friday. Yahoo Finance reported Nasdaq futures tripped a circuit breaker on the news. Nearly −4% premarket Tuesday (Nvidia newsroom; CNBC; Yahoo Finance; Globe and Mail, 23–24 Nov).
Anthropic (ANT) — −1.43% to $87.64 Monday, range about $84.61–$94.24, volume about 253M shares (Yahoo Finance history; Investing.com, 23 Nov).

Futures — Tuesday 5:50 a.m. ET: Nasdaq-100 −1.21%, S&P 500 −0.50%, Dow −0.14%; later snapshots smaller, around S&P −0.45% (TipRanks; CNBC, 24 Nov). European stocks slipping as well (Globe and Mail, 24 Nov).
deals: CrowdStrike / Zscaler — all-stock deal valuing Zscaler at about $43.9 billion; 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share, about a 34% premium to the 20 Nov close (Bloomberg; TipRanks, 23 Nov).

Alta Equipment Group / Jackson Group Peterbilt — dealership assets for $272.5 million plus a net tangible asset adjustment; 34 dealerships in eight western states; subject to stockholder and financing approvals (TipRanks, 23 Nov).
Rosemont Pharmaceuticals / Aytu BioPharma — $2.70 per share cash tender offer, a 51.7% premium (Lawrence, Evans & Co., 23 Nov).
Merck KGaA / Rapid Micro Biosystems — $0.75 per share cash tender offer (Lawrence, Evans & Co., 23 Nov).
macro: S&P Global flash PMIs, November — manufacturing 54.5 from 54.9; services 54.7 from 56.1 against about 55.7–55.8 expected; composite 54.6 from 55.9, a four-month low (FXStreet; investingLive; S&P Global, 23 Nov).

Williams (New York Fed) — expects PCE inflation to end 2026 at 3.5%, slow to just above 2% next year and reach 2% in 2028; growth 2.75% in 2026 and 2027; higher rates likely “over time,” no call for dramatic action. Next FOMC 8–9 Dec (NY Fed Teller Window; CNBC; Reuters via Yahoo, 23 Nov).
Rest of week — Wednesday 25 Nov: October PCE and Q3 GDP second estimate at 8:30 ET; markets closed Thursday; 1:00 p.m. ET close Friday (heygotrade; TradingKey, 23 Nov).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: A one-day 4.7% S&P rebound driven by a single company’s leadership news, into a holiday-shortened week with a December rate hike fully priced.
regime.sizing: Tuesday’s early futures pullback leaves open how much of Monday’s move holds before Wednesday’s PCE and GDP.

secondOrder: Monday’s gains were again uneven, this time in reverse: the Nasdaq rose more than twice as much as the Dow, mirroring Friday’s split. Treasury yields barely moved on a near-5% equity rally, and Anthropic fell on a day most AI-linked shares rose. Observations, not forecasts.

scorecard.text: The prior brief reported S&P 500 futures up about 2.2–2.8% early Monday and left open whether the bounce would hold through the open. It held and widened: the S&P 500 closed +4.73% and the Nasdaq +6.51% (StockTitan; Motley Fool, 23 Nov).

The prior brief carried a services flash PMI consensus of 55.8 and manufacturing 54.6 (FXStreet). Services printed 54.7, about a point below, and manufacturing 54.5; the brief listed consensus, not a forecast, but anyone reading it as the likely print was wrong on services (FXStreet; investingLive, 23 Nov).

The prior brief listed New York Fed President Williams speaking Monday evening from a single source; he spoke, saying inflation remains too high and rates likely rise over time (CNBC; NY Fed, 23 Nov).
The prior brief put October PCE and the Q3 GDP second estimate on Wednesday and Dell after Tuesday’s close; both confirmed by Tuesday-morning calendars (mlq.ai; TradingKey, 24 Nov).
